newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT - Raimon rated underperform.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Raimon rated underperform.

text.p: Raimon Land, a major developer of middle and low priced condominiums, was given an underperform rating on Tuesday by Thaimex Finance and Securities Plc due to its doubtful financing, weak earnings and unclear future.
"Following a company visit, it seems to us that in a best-case scenario with all luck on its side, the company can at most hope for mere survival with a tiny net profit," Thaimex said in a report.

"If anything goes wrong, however, whether (it be) a slowdown in sales, a currency devaluation, or most importantly, a failure of one of the big asset sales, the company will have nowhere to hide," it said.
The report added that Raimon Land's survival strategy is to cut costs, mostly by reducing personnel costs and lowering the sale price of its properties.
But it said the country's economic slump would continue to pressure the company's outlook as in the case of many other property companies.
Raimon Land reported a 40 million baht ($1.6 million) loss during the first quarter of 1997 compared with a 20 million baht loss for the whole 1996.

Despite first quarter loss, Thaimex said Raimon Land may be able to make small profit in 1997 due to quicker transfers of ownership as the year goes progresses and one-time gains on the sale of assets.
The company is now trying to sell three major assets, which could fetch 3.15 billion baht, within this year.
"But even in the best case, net profit will only reach 25 million baht," the Thaimex Finance report said.

"For 1998, the lack of asset sales together with a slightly weaker margin means that even though sales will be larger and interest much lower, net profit will come in lower at 17 million baht," it added.
Raimon closed up 0.30 baht at 4.90 baht on Monday. The Thai market is closed today for a Buddhist holiday.
